title: FlashAttention: Fast Transformer Training with Long Sequences
excerpt: Tri Dao details how parallelizing FlashAttention over the sequence dimension keeps GPUs saturated at long context, making 8k-token GPT training up to 2.7x faster than an optimized baseline while computing exact attention.
author: Tri Dao
coverAlt: FlashAttention forward and backward pass parallelization diagram

title: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning
excerpt: FlashAttention-2 rewrites the attention kernel with better work partitioning between warps and thread blocks and fewer non-matmul FLOPs, reaching up to 2x the speed of the original FlashAttention and 72% of peak A100 throughput.
author: Tri Dao
coverAlt: FlashAttention versus FlashAttention-2 work partitioning diagram

title: How to Scale Your Model
excerpt: Google DeepMind engineers turn LLM scaling from alchemy into arithmetic: a book-length treatment of rooflines, TPU and GPU architecture, collective communication, and every major parallelism strategy for training and inference.
author: Jacob Austin, Sholto Douglas, Roy Frostig, et al.
coverAlt: How to Scale Your Model book cover artwork

title: Transformer Inference Arithmetic
excerpt: Kipply derives a back-of-the-envelope performance model for transformer inference, using KV cache size, weight memory, FLOPs, and communication costs to predict latency and throughput before running a single benchmark.
author: Carol Chen (kipply)
coverAlt: Transformer inference arithmetic article cover

title: Making Deep Learning Go Brrrr From First Principles
excerpt: Horace He splits deep learning performance into compute-bound, memory-bandwidth-bound, and overhead-bound regimes, showing how to diagnose which one you are in and why optimizations like operator fusion only pay off in the right regime.
author: Horace He
coverAlt: GPUs go brrr illustration from the article

title: General and Scalable Parallelization for Neural Networks
excerpt: Google Research introduces GSPMD, an XLA compiler pass that expands lightweight tensor sharding annotations into full SPMD parallelization, letting a single program express data, model, and pipeline parallelism across thousands of accelerators.
author: Yuanzhong Xu and Yanping Huang
coverAlt: GSPMD parallelization article cover

title: Looking Back at Speculative Decoding
excerpt: Yaniv Leviathan and colleagues recount the origin of speculative decoding, explaining how draft-then-verify sampling emits several tokens per serial step without changing the output distribution, and how the idea spread through production LLM serving.
author: Yaniv Leviathan, Matan Kalman, and Yossi Matias
coverAlt: Speculative decoding retrospective article cover

title: Mastering LLM Techniques: Inference Optimization
excerpt: A single reference that maps the LLM inference stack end to end: prefill versus decode, KV caching, batching, attention variants like MQA/GQA and FlashAttention, PagedAttention, quantization, and model parallelism strategies.
author: Shashank Verma and Neal Vaidya
coverAlt: LLM inference optimization overview graphic

title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning using PEFT
excerpt: Hugging Face introduces the PEFT library, showing how LoRA, prefix tuning, and prompt tuning adapt billion-parameter models by training a small fraction of weights, with checkpoints measured in megabytes instead of tens of gigabytes.
author: Sourab Mangrulkar and Sayak Paul
coverAlt: PEFT library announcement thumbnail

title: Making LLMs Even More Accessible with bitsandbytes, 4-bit Quantization and QLoRA
excerpt: The QLoRA release explained: 4-bit NF4 quantization, double quantization, and paged optimizers in bitsandbytes let a 65B-parameter model be fine-tuned on a single 48GB GPU while matching 16-bit fine-tuning quality.
author: Younes Belkada, Tim Dettmers, et al.
coverAlt: bitsandbytes 4-bit quantization thumbnail

title: Improving LoRA: Implementing Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation (DoRA) from Scratch
excerpt: Sebastian Raschka implements LoRA and DoRA in plain PyTorch from scratch, showing how DoRA's decomposition of weights into magnitude and direction can beat LoRA even with half the rank.
author: Sebastian Raschka
coverAlt: LoRA and DoRA from scratch article cover

title: Inference Economics of Language Models
excerpt: Ege Erdil builds a first-principles economic model of LLM inference covering arithmetic, memory bandwidth, network bandwidth, and latency constraints, deriving cost-versus-speed Pareto frontiers and why serial speedups get expensive fast.
author: Ege Erdil
coverAlt: Inference economics of language models report banner

title: ThunderKittens: A Simple Embedded DSL for AI Kernels
excerpt: Hazy Research argues that GPUs want simple abstractions: ThunderKittens is an embedded CUDA DSL built around 16x16 tiles that makes attention and other AI kernels easier to write while staying competitive with hand-tuned libraries.
author: Benjamin Spector, Aaryan Singhal, Simran Arora, et al.
coverAlt: ThunderKittens blog hero illustration

title: How Our New Control Red Team is Stress-Testing Frontier Monitors
excerpt: UK AISI's Control Red Team shares early lessons from red-teaming the internal monitors frontier AI companies use to catch misbehaving models, and lays out the open problems in making those monitors robust to adversarial pressure.
author: UK AI Security Institute
coverAlt: UK AISI control red team article cover

title: Prioritizing Threats for AI Control
excerpt: Ryan Greenblatt maps the space of threats that AI control should defend against, arguing that control resources should be allocated across scheming risk scenarios by likelihood and severity rather than spread evenly over all conceivable failures.
author: Ryan Greenblatt
coverAlt: Prioritizing threats for AI control article cover

title: The Building Blocks of Interpretability
excerpt: Olah and colleagues combine feature visualization, attribution, and matrix factorization into composable interfaces for looking inside neural networks, establishing a foundational grammar for modern interpretability tooling.
author: Chris Olah, Arvind Satyanarayan, et al.
coverAlt: Building blocks of interpretability feature visualization thumbnail

title: Thread: Circuits
excerpt: The Distill Circuits thread argues that neural networks contain understandable, reusable circuits of features, documenting curve detectors and other structures weight by weight in InceptionV1 as an 'open science' interpretability program.
author: Nick Cammarata, Shan Carter, Gabriel Goh, Chris Olah, et al.
coverAlt: Distill circuits thread thumbnail

title: A Discussion of 'Adversarial Examples Are Not Bugs, They Are Features'
excerpt: A structured scientific exchange around the claim that adversarial examples exploit non-robust but genuinely predictive features, with six response essays and author replies that sharpen exactly what the result does and does not show.
author: Logan Engstrom, Justin Gilmer, Gabriel Goh, et al.
coverAlt: Adversarial examples discussion article thumbnail

title: How Undesired Goals Can Arise with Correct Rewards
excerpt: DeepMind researchers separate goal misgeneralisation from specification gaming, giving concrete RL and LLM examples where an agent trained with a correct reward signal still learns to pursue the wrong goal out of distribution.
author: Rohin Shah, Victoria Krakovna, Vikrant Varma, and Zachary Kenton
coverAlt: Goal misgeneralisation article cover

title: Deliberative Alignment: Reasoning Enables Safer Language Models
excerpt: OpenAI describes deliberative alignment, which teaches o-series models the text of safety specifications and trains them to reason explicitly over those specifications at inference time, improving both refusal precision and jailbreak robustness.
author: OpenAI
coverAlt: Deliberative alignment article cover

title: Simple Probes Can Catch Sleeper Agents
excerpt: Anthropic shows that simple linear probes on residual-stream activations can detect backdoored 'sleeper agent' models about to defect, working surprisingly well even with generic contrast prompts unrelated to the backdoor behavior.
author: Anthropic Alignment Science Team
coverAlt: Sleeper agent probes article cover

title: An Off Switch for Dual-Use Knowledge in AI Models
excerpt: Anthropic and AE Studio introduce GRAM, which routes gradients from dual-use training data into dedicated removable modules, so capabilities like virology knowledge can be deleted at deployment while general abilities stay intact.
author: Anthropic
coverAlt: Off switch for dual-use knowledge article cover

title: A 'Diff' Tool for AI: Finding Behavioral Differences in New Models
excerpt: Anthropic Fellows build a diff tool that compares the internal features of two models and flags behaviors exclusive to one of them, surfacing switches like censorship or copyright-refusal features that black-box testing would likely miss.
author: Anthropic
coverAlt: Diff tool for AI models article cover

title: An Early Warning System for Novel AI Risks
excerpt: DeepMind proposes an early-warning framework for frontier risk: evaluate models separately for dangerous capabilities and for alignment, and feed the results into training, deployment, and security decisions before harm can occur.
author: Toby Shevlane
coverAlt: Early warning system for novel AI risks article cover
